definitions.explanation: One of the twenty first teeth a child grows, which fall out from about the age of six and are replaced by the permanent teeth ({永久歯|えいきゅうし}).

examples.japanese: {乳歯|にゅうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}けた→抜ける：02385_nukeru⟧。
⟦{娘|むすめ}→娘：02263_musume⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{初|はじ}めて→初めて：02932_hajimete⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{乳歯|にゅうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|は}えた→生える：02392_haeru⟧。
examples.english: My daughter's first baby tooth came in.

examples.japanese: {乳歯|にゅうし}⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦いずれ→いずれ：01789_izure⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}ける→抜ける：02385_nukeru⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{虫歯|むしば}→虫歯：00299_mushiba⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ならない→なる：01970_naru⟧よう⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{歯磨|はみが}き→歯磨き：03137_hamigaki⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{大切|たいせつ}→大切：01456_taisetsu⟧だ。
examples.english: Baby teeth will fall out eventually, but brushing them to prevent cavities is still important.

notes:
⟦{乳|にゅう}→乳：28296_nyuu⟧ (milk) + {歯|し} (tooth, in its Sino-Japanese reading). Children usually say ⟦{歯|は}→歯：00778_ha⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}けた→抜ける：02385_nukeru⟧ rather than the word itself. Same sound as ⟦{入試|にゅうし}→入試：04705_nyuushi⟧ (entrance exam); context tells them apart.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {乳歯|にゅうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{抜|ぬ}ける→抜ける：02385_nukeru⟧: a baby tooth comes out
- {乳歯|にゅうし}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{生|は}える→生える：02392_haeru⟧: a baby tooth comes in
- {乳歯|にゅうし}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{永久歯|えいきゅうし}→永久歯：33511_eikyuushi⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{生|は}え{変|か}わる→生え変わる：32223_haekawaru⟧: baby teeth are replaced by permanent ones

CULTURAL NOTE:
By tradition a lost lower tooth is thrown onto the roof and an upper one under the floor, so that the new tooth grows straight toward the old one.
